chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hisham ibn al-Hakam said:
I asked him about a man who manumits his slave on condition of service (tadbir), is he allowed to take him back? He said, 'Yes, he is in the position of the will (wasiyyah).'

key_terms.يَرْجِعَ فِيهِ: To take him back / reclaim him
key_terms.يُدَبِّرُ: He manumits on condition of service (tadbir)

ai.seo_question: Can a master take back a slave after freeing them with the condition of service (tadbir)?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, highlighting the juristic consensus that a master's right to revoke 'tadbir' (conditional manumission) is legally analogous to the revocability of a will (*wasiyyah*). This comparison underscores the master's retained ownership rights during the service period, distinguishing it from immediate, irrevocable freedom. The ruling reflects the practical flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding the economic and social dynamics of slavery in early Islamic society.
